parameter_semantics: target_object selects the observed blue pose and blue translation anchor; destination_goal selects the observed blue-goal point and goal anchor; context_object selects the observed buffered-red pose and red anchor; source_region selects the observed initially-red region used to compute causal blue transport progress. Poses and points are in world coordinates, positions and learned offsets are metres, orientation is world-frame 6D, and training binds blue, blue_goal, red, and red_goal.
output_semantics: Each slot is [anchor-relative dx,dy,dz in world metres; world TCP rotation as the first two rotation-matrix columns; native gripper scalar; blue,blue_goal,red anchor weights]. Training anchor weights are one-hot labels selected from that slot's causal pre-action geometry: red when TCP is clearly nearer red, otherwise blue before 0.72 source-to-goal progress, otherwise blue_goal. Decode clips and normalizes the three learned weights to a simplex, blends freshly observed world landmark translations, adds the learned offset, projects 6D orientation by Gram-Schmidt, and calls panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh qpos. Slots represent t-1 through t+14; execution uses slots 1 through 8 beginning at current t. No predicted-state accumulation or scripted phase transition is used.

conversion_check.description: For supervised labels, the one-hot landmark weight selects the same per-slot pre-action anchor subtracted by encode_targets, so fresh-anchor composition exactly recovers the demonstrated command FK position; 6D projection recovers its rotation. The independent check compares world TCP position, rotation angle, and gripper while allowing nonunique IK. Sampled weights and rotations use the declared simplex and Gram-Schmidt projections.

cut_relation: All actions in all twelve assigned slices are supervised. The representation retains predecessor red release through blue approach/close/lift, the complete blue-to-blue-goal relocation, and successor blue release through buffered-red approach/close/lift; only Cartesian coordinates and an action-supervised landmark label change.
